$comment: RAAST Hebrew (he) language profile. Consumed by the raast CLI prose rules and referenced by skills/rtl-typography. Hebrew is the third major RTL script: letters are separate (not cursive), Western digits are standard in prose, and gershayim/geresh/maqaf carry the orthographic duties Persian/Arabic solve differently.
name: Hebrew

numerals.unicode_range_note: Modern Hebrew prose uses Western digits 0-9 exclusively. Arabic-Indic variants (٠-٩ / ۰-۹) are invalid in Hebrew text.

punctuation.quotes_note: Straight or curly Latin quotes are the modern norm; guillemets appear in translated/legacy texts.
punctuation.usage_notes: Standard Latin marks are valid in modern Hebrew prose. Use gershayim ״ INSIDE acronyms (e.g., רא״ם), geresh ׳ for abbreviations and foreign phonetics, and maqaf ־ for hyphenated compounds where typography allows — plain hyphen-minus is accepted on the web.

letters.script_note: Hebrew letters are separate glyphs (not cursive/joined like Arabic) — no letter joining ever occurs and no ZWNJ affix compounds exist.
letters.nikud_note: Vowel points (nikud) sit above/below the line: body line-height must leave vertical room or points clip and collide.

typography.letter_spacing_note: Non-zero letter-spacing on Hebrew shatters word cohesion and breaks final-form letter rhythm (ך ם ן ף ץ). Justified text must use word spacing, never letter spacing.

dates.calendar: hebrew (lunar) for cultural content; gregorian for product UI
dates.intl_tag_note: Use ca=hebrew for Hebrew-calendar dates (holidays, memorial days); Intl falls back per platform support.
dates.months_note: Leap years split אדר into אדר א׳ and אדר ב׳ — format month names through Intl, never hardcode.

bidi_marks.notes: Latin words, URLs, emails, phone numbers and code snippets inside Hebrew prose must be isolated; never strip U+200E/U+200F marks.
